answer: Agents lock a slashable stake per identity, and voting weight flows from that stake, not from headcount, so minting extra names buys no extra influence. Each identity carries a hardware-signed attestation that cannot be cloned onto another machine. A Sybil farmer therefore funds every fake agent with real locked capital, and if two clones ever attest to conflicting ledgers the bond is slashed. Even at a token-price nadir, sprawling across a barren tundra of fake wallets stays costly: each new meadow of votes needs its own stake, and one double-sign can wipe out the whole position.
